fix(watchers): every directory watch is judged against the disk on the delivery owner's period (brandon-unfiled-3248.erwl) (#514)

* fix(watchers): every directory watch is judged against the disk on the delivery owner's period (brandon-unfiled-3248.erwl)

A directory watch binds an inode. A strict ancestor of a watched directory
renamed away and another tree put at its path reports nothing to the handle:
inotify reports a directory's own removal or self-move, never its parent's,
so the handle stays listening, bound to a folder no longer at its path, and
the config cache, which has no period, never re-derives its key. Edits at the
path go unheard and no fault shows.

The registry's one rule that a directory watch names the folder at its path
now runs over every directory watch on the file-event delivery owner's
period, which the daemon already keeps time by: a deaf directory is opened
again and one whose path holds another folder is reopened in place, telling
every slot on it an unknown window, through which the config cache, the git
provider, watch_file sources and the plugin storage owner recover as they
already do.

The period is the one owned bound on retrying a deaf directory, so a kept
follow retries nothing. The deaf-only retry a kept follow ran, its
failed-window gate, and the window threaded to it through the config cache,
the git repo state and watch_file sources are removed.

* fix(watchers): a reload that keeps its watch is what retries nothing, and the git watch asks for its pass directly (brandon-unfiled-3248.erwl)

The memory sentence and the judgment's comment claimed the period was the only retry of a deaf directory; an acquire judges the directories it names too. The git provider's heard wrapper had no job left once the failed window went.

* test(render-cache): the parent-rename test proves the judgment closed a handle before any window lands (brandon-unfiled-3248.erwl)

On macOS the watch follows the path and would hear the write by itself, so the entry reading the new tree proved nothing about the judgment there. The synchronous close is the reopen, on both platforms.
